space with interpretability measures based on hyperbolic geometry, to define
anisotropic latent diffusion processes for graphs. Then, we propose a
geometrically latent diffusion process that is constrained by both radial and

add_method_texts.title:
Stochastic Conditional Diffusion Models for Robust Semantic Image
  Synthesis
add_method_texts.summary:
Semantic image synthesis (SIS) is a task to generate realistic images
corresponding to semantic maps (labels). However, in real-world applications,
SIS often encounters noisy user inputs. To address this, we propose Stochastic
Conditional Diffusion Model (SCDM), which is a robust conditional diffusion
model that features novel forward and generation processes tailored for SIS
with noisy labels. It enhances robustness by stochastically perturbing the
semantic label maps through Label Diffusion, which diffuses the labels with
discrete diffusion. Through the diffusion of labels, the noisy and clean
semantic maps become similar as the timestep increases, eventually becoming
identical at $t=T$. This facilitates the generation of an image close to a
clean image, enabling robust generation. Furthermore, we propose a class-wise
noise schedule to differentially diffuse the labels depending on the class. We
demonstrate that the proposed method generates high-quality samples through
extensive experiments and analyses on benchmark datasets, including a novel
experimental setup simulating human errors during real-world applications. Code
is available at https://github.com/mlvlab/SCDM.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces Stochastic Conditional Diffusion Model (SCDM), a novel diffusion model designed to enhance robustness in semantic image synthesis (SIS) when dealing with noisy semantic label maps. It incorporates Label Diffusion, a discrete diffusion process for labels, and introduces a class-wise noise schedule to improve the generation quality of smaller and rarer classes. The paper also provides theoretical analyses and introduces a new noisy SIS benchmark to assess generation performance under noisy conditions.
add_method_texts.methodology: The SCDM employs a conditional diffusion model with novel forward and generation processes. It uses Label Diffusion, a discrete diffusion process with label masking, to stochastically perturb semantic label maps. A class-wise noise schedule is incorporated to differentially diffuse labels based on class. The model is trained using a hybrid loss function, and classifier-free guidance with extrapolation is used during sampling.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The method is evaluated on the ADE20K dataset and a newly introduced noisy SIS benchmark, including downsampled semantic maps, edge-masked labels, and randomly corrupted masks. The performance is measured using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU). Ablation studies are conducted to assess the impact of different components.
add_method_texts.limitations: One limitation is the potential for the model to ignore user intentions by generating clean images even when noisy images are desired. Another limitation mentioned is that the model cannot dynamically learn the optimal noise schedules for labels.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring methods to control faithfulness to the semantic maps, allowing users to generate noisy images if desired. Another direction is to develop mechanisms for dynamically learning optimal noise schedules for labels, which could increase the flexibility and power of semantic image synthesis.
